learning_outcomes.description: Read, interpret, and discuss world literature at university level.
Learn how literature from diverse cultures can engage productively with diverse communities and contribute to positive social change.
Present your analysis and research by demonstrating key disciplinary skills such as human-authored critical reading, textual interpretation, original analysis, and independent research.

assessments.due_date:
Week 2 - Week 13

Each week in tutorials students will complete a 10 minute writing task in response to a question based on that week's readings.
assessments.task_description:
Each week in tutorials we will set a 10 minute writing task, in which you write a response to a question based on that week's readings. Responses will be submitted through an online portal in Blackboard. These are marked on a pass/fail basis and can earn you 1% towards your final grade.

Rationale: Consistent preparation and participation lead to better learning outcomes and more productive and enjoyable learning experiences. Through participation, humanities students gain a highly valued and distinctive skill set in human-authored critical thinking, discipline mastery, evidence-based learning, and collaboration. These skills are required by many workplaces. The ability to write on a set topic and within a short time frame is a valuable academic and vocational skill, and it helps you to track your learning and prepare for written assessment tasks. Finally, this assessment item provides basic weekly feedback throughout the semester.
assessments.submission_guidelines: Responses will be submitted through an online portal in Blackboard and must be submitted during your tutorial.
assessments.deferral_or_extension: You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.
assessments.late_submission: You will receive a mark of 0 if this assessment is submitted late.
assessments.additional_info: You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.

assessments.task_description: Essay 2 requires students to engage with scholarly criticism and selected literary texts from weeks 7-10 in the course. Essay topics will be made available in Blackboard during semester. The essay must be correctly formatted with a Works Cited in MLA 9th edition, guidelines for which are accessible through the UQ Library. Care should be given to expression, punctuation, and grammar.

assessments.task_description:
This assessment task will require you to prepare and deliver a (maximum) 5-minute oral presentation on Patricia Grace’s Baby No-Eyes and decolonisation. This task also gives you the opportunity to reflect critically on key issues studied in the course. Your presentation must focus on Baby No-Eyes, but you may mention in your presentation other texts and ideas that you have studied in this course that demonstrate how your disciplinary knowledge and skills have developed over the semester. 

Students will sign up for an allocated time during the examination period to meet with course staff and deliver a 4-5 minute presentation based on an oral assessment guide that will be available in Blackboard. Following your presentation, up to two additional questions will be asked to enable the student to amplify or clarify their presentation.

We will build oral skills and confidence throughout the tutorials.

Note: presentations will be recorded (audio only).
